title: Verifier‑Grounded NetConfig‑Semantic Study (preregistered estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; shared_initial_candidate semantics)
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) that evaluates a narrow, preregistered estimand: the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate generation semantics. Using a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and N = 120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks we observed baseline = 120/120 verifier passes and guarded (gpt‑5‑mini, shared_initial seed_0) = 120/120 verifier passes (paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00,0.00]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0). All execution and scoring artifacts (model calls, canonical shared candidates, and per‑episode validator traces) are published in the submission bundle (representative files: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36..., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57f..., execution/execution_manifest.json). We show—using those same archived artifacts—why the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics produce a degenerate paired contingency and we provide runnable, artifact‑grounded modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmatory design, validator diversification, and expanded task heterogeneity) that preserve reproducibility while answering the operational question practitioners typically need: independent per‑condition generative reliability.

sections.introduction: Automated translation of operator intent into device configuration is a core NetOps problem where correctness and transient safety matter: incorrect sequences can break reachability, violate ACLs, or create unsafe transient states. Deterministic offline validators (reachability/ACL/routing analyzers) are the accepted operational oracle for pre‑deployment checks (see Batfish evolution; Brown et al., 2023, doi:10.1145/3603269.3604866). We preregistered a narrowly specified confirmatory estimand—paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline—under explicitly frozen generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate) to test whether a deterministic validator treats identical canonical candidates differently across two scoring conditions. The present paper (1) publishes the exact artifacts and SHA‑256 fingerprints needed for byte‑for‑byte reruns; (2) reports the preregistered confirmatory outcome (baseline = 120/120; guarded = 120/120; paired difference = 0.00; CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar p = 1.0) using archived traces; and (3) diagnoses, using those same artifacts, why the preregistered design produced a degenerate contingency and how to rerun the pipeline to answer the operational question of independent generative reliability.
sections.related_work: Verifier‑grounded evaluation. Prior work couples LLM or template generators to deterministic verifiers in a generate–validate–repair architecture; empirical factors that matter include sampling semantics (single canonical vs independent sampling), repair budgets (bounded iterations), and validator scope (syntactic vs reachability/ACL/routing checks). Recent studies emphasize that orchestration and feedback often dominate repair effectiveness and that most repair gains accrue in the first few iterations (see iterative‑repair analyses in the evidence corpus). Reproducibility and full artifact publication are recurring recommendations in this literature; incomplete artifact release obstructs deterministic reruns and contamination analysis. Our contribution is an evidence‑complete preregistered run with exhaustive traces and hashes enabling deterministic reproduction and post‑hoc diagnosis.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. We preregistered CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1 before observing model outputs. Key frozen items: N = 120 paired tasks (40 per topology class), deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, model = declared gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2...), generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one canonical LLM candidate generated per task and reused across both scoring conditions), initial canonical seed_0, and analysis = paired_binary_analysis_v1 with bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). All of the above and every artifact path and SHA‑256 are in the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json). Task synthesis. Tasks were programmatically generated from a deterministic template bank (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5). Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, an explicit required_sequence, and workflow_policies (for example: must_be_down_for_fields, minimum_active_in_groups). Representative examples with exact artifact locations are included in the bundle (see execution/task_manifest.jsonl and the representative examples under artifact_examples). Scoring and validator traces. Each candidate was parsed and deterministically scored by deterministic_netops_validator_v5; per‑episode JSON traces were archived under execution/scoring/*.json (representative: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57f...). Analysis. The primary estimator is the mean over pairs of (guarded_i − baseline_i). We computed a 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) and an exact McNemar two‑sided test on the paired 2×2 table. The full analysis artifacts are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c..., analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256 9c77c96f...).
sections.results: Confirmatory counts and tests. All preregistered confirmatory episodes completed (planned_episode_count = 240; completed_episode_count = 240; model_calls_used = 120; failed_episode_count = 0). The deterministic validator accepted every canonical candidate under both conditions: baseline_success_count = 120/120; guarded_success_count = 120/120. Paired contingency: n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Paired estimate = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00,0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Representative validator trace excerpt (archived): execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json shows parsed_command_count = 4 and validation_after.valid = true; the canonical candidate is archived at execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36...). Why the confirmatory contrast collapsed. The archived artifacts show two preregistered design choices that deterministically produce the observed degenerate contingency: (A) generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate — a single canonical candidate per task was generated and reused verbatim for both scoring conditions; (B) task templates encode exact required_sequences and workflow_policies that the canonical candidates directly satisfy. Because the validator is deterministic, identical inputs produce identical pass/fail outputs. The causal chain is auditable in the published artifacts: the shared candidate files (execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt) match the per‑episode scoring traces (execution/scoring/*), which together explain n_11 = 120.
sections.discussion: Interpretation and operational meaning. The confirmatory statistics are correct for the preregistered estimand (verifier‑consistency under identical inputs) but do not address independent generative reliability—the operational quantity operators usually need (probability that independently sampled LLM outputs satisfy verifier constraints). The difference is methodological and critical: shared_initial_candidate isolates validator determinism and scoring reproducibility; independent_per_condition sampling or multi‑seed per condition estimates generative stochastic reliability. Runnable artifact‑grounded modifications. The archived pipeline permits deterministic reruns that answer the operational question without new unexplained artifacts: (1) independent_per_condition rerun: generate separate seeds per condition per task and rescore using deterministic_netops_validator_v5; (2) multi‑seed confirmatory design: K ≥ 3 independent seeds per condition per task to estimate per‑condition pass probability with bootstrap CIs; (3) validator diversification: add an independent verifier and report intersection/union pass rates to reduce validator–task coupling. All inputs, seeds, model configuration, and scoring harness paths required to run these reruns deterministically are present in the bundle (execution/model_configuration.json; execution/provider_calls/*.json; execution/call_cache/*). Threats to validity (artifact‑visible). Internal validity: shared_initial design removed generation variance intentionally and thus precluded testing independent generative reliability. Construct validity: template‑aligned tasks and a single deterministic validator may overestimate success relative to open intents. External validity: single model and synthetic tasks limit generalization. Contamination note. We ran preregistered string‑overlap contamination heuristics and recorded results (analysis/contamination_summary.csv); no confirmatory items flagged under the chosen thresholds, but absence of a heuristic flag is not definitive proof of zero pretraining exposure. Value of exhaustive artifacts. Publishing provider traces, canonical candidate hashes, per‑episode validator traces, and the full execution manifest (with SHA‑256s) enables byte‑for‑byte reproduction, precise contamination auditing, and deterministic reruns under alternative sampling semantics.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, verifier‑grounded paired experiment and released a complete artifact bundle enabling deterministic reproduction. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics both the deterministic template baseline and the gpt‑5‑mini guarded condition validated on all N = 120 tasks (120/120 each). Archived evidence demonstrates that identical canonical candidates per pair plus template‑tight task constraints caused the degenerate paired outcome. The confirmatory result therefore answers the narrow preregistered estimand correctly but does not estimate independent LLM generative reliability. We publish runnable, artifact‑grounded modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed replication, validator diversification, task heterogeneity expansion) that preserve reproducibility while producing informative operational comparisons. All execution and analysis artifacts—including the immutable master prompt reference (provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and the preregistration SHA‑256—are included to permit exact audit and follow‑up experiments.

limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, reducing independence between conditions and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not included in the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
